flags.where: Prompt, first paragraph ('the formal organization of the Royal Society of London in 1662')
flags.detail: The Royal Society was formally constituted at Gresham College on 28 November 1660, when the group agreed to found a 'College for the Promoting of Physico-Mathematicall Experimentall Learning' and began keeping a journal book and electing members. 1662 is the date of the first royal charter (incorporation), not the formal organization of the society. The prompt should say 'chartered in 1662' or 'organized in 1660 and chartered in 1662'. The sample response's (C) phrasing ('later became the Royal Society... got a royal charter') is consistent with the correct chronology.

flags.where: Prompt, introductory paragraph ('the formal organization of the Royal Society of London in 1662') and (A) ('before 1662')
flags.detail: The Royal Society was formally founded at a meeting at Gresham College on 28 November 1660; 1662 is the date of its first royal charter (incorporation). The Society itself and standard references date its founding/organization to 1660. Stating that it was 'formally organized' in 1662 conflates chartering with founding; rephrase as 'before it received its royal charter in 1662' or use 1660.

flags.where: Prompt, opening paragraph ('the formal organization of the Royal Society of London in 1662') and part (A) ('before 1662')
flags.detail: The Royal Society was formally organized in November 1660, when the group meeting at Gresham College resolved to found a 'College for the Promoting of Physico-Mathematical Experimental Learning,' drew up a membership list and began keeping minutes. 1662 is the date of the first royal charter of incorporation, not of the society's formal organization. The prompt should either say 'founded in 1660 and chartered in 1662' or refer to 1660; as written it misdates the founding and may mislead students about which meetings count as 'before' the Society.
